findings.claim: The model answer says a wine must have been DOC for ten years before it can be considered for DOCG, and the accept list takes only ten years or a decade.
findings.because: Ten years was the rule under D.Lgs. 61/2010. The Testo Unico del Vino (Legge 12 dicembre 2016 n. 238, in force from 12 January 2017), art. 33, cut it to seven: 'Il riconoscimento della DOCG è riservato ai vini già riconosciuti a DOC da almeno sette anni'. The same article keeps the rung below at five years as IGT, so the explanation's 'shorter clock' line still holds. A candidate who learns ten years answers wrong under current law, and the grader refuses the correct answer.
findings.fix: ans: "Seven years"; accept: ["seven years","7 years","seven","7","at least seven years","at least 7 years","minimum seven years","minimum 7 years","seven years as a doc","7 years as a doc","seven years at doc level","7 years at doc level","seven years at doc","7 years at doc","at least seven years as a doc","at least 7 years as a doc"]; exp: replace "checked for a decade" with "checked for seven years (ten until the 2016 Testo Unico del Vino, Law 238/2016, cut it)"
findings.verifyReason: The finding holds, and the proposed fix is correct. I opened the current text of Law 238/2016 (the Testo Unico del Vino), art. 33, on Normattiva. It reads: "Il riconoscimento della DOCG è riservato ai vini già riconosciuti a DOC da almeno sette anni". So under current law a wine must have been DOC for at least seven years before it can be considered for DOCG. The same article sets the rung below at five years as IGT ("a IGT da almeno cinque anni"), so the explanation's "shorter clock" line is still true, since five is less than seven. D.Lgs. 61/2010 art. 8 is where the older ten-year rule sat. Normattiva marks that article as repealed by L. 238/2016, which in force from 12 January 2017. I could not display its repealed text, so the "ten years before 2017" point rests on the repeal notice and on how the rule is commonly described. The question's answer, "Ten years", is therefore outdated. Its accept list takes only ten or a decade, so it refuses the answer that is correct today. The examiner's fix sets the answer to seven years, accepts the usual phrasings of seven, and notes the pre-2016 figure in the explanation.
findings.finalFix: ans: "Seven years"; accept: ["seven years","7 years","seven","7","at least seven years","at least 7 years","minimum seven years","minimum 7 years","seven years minimum","7 years minimum","seven years as a doc","7 years as a doc","seven years at doc level","7 years at doc level","seven years at doc","7 years at doc","at least seven years as a doc","at least 7 years as a doc","at least seven years at doc level","at least 7 years at doc level"]; exp: "The waiting period is what stops the top rank being handed to a name invented last season: the wine has to have existed, been made to a rulebook and been checked for seven years (ten until the 2016 Testo Unico del Vino, Law 238/2016, cut it) before anyone will look at it. The rung below works the same way on a shorter clock, five years as an IGT, so a new denomination climbs the ladder rather than stepping onto it halfway up."

question.q: Italy will not consider a wine for its highest denomination until it has served a stated minimum at the tier below. How long is that apprenticeship?
accept: at least ten years as a doc
at least ten years at doc level
at least ten years at doc
at least 10 years as a doc
at least 10 years at doc level
minimum ten years as a doc
minimum ten years at doc level
ten years minimum as a doc
ten years minimum at doc level
question.exp: The waiting period is what stops the top rank being handed to a name invented last season: the wine has to have existed, been made to a rulebook and been checked for a decade before anyone will look at it. The rung below works the same way on a shorter clock, so a new denomination climbs the ladder rather than stepping onto it halfway up.
